entry.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; 2026 Commercial Quota Harvested for the State of Maine — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
entry.content: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.

entry.title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Framework Adjustment 7 to the Atlantic Spiny Dogfish Fishery Management Plan — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
entry.content: NMFS proposes measures included in Framework Adjustment 7 to the Spiny Dogfish Fishery Management Plan (FMP), as recommended by the Mid-Atlantic and New England Fishery Management Councils. Framework 7 proposes fishing year 2026 and projected 2027 specifications, which would establish allowable harvest levels for the spiny dogfish fishery to prevent overfishing while enabling optimum yield based on the best scientific information available. Framework 7 also proposes changes to the Atlantic spiny dogfish accountability measures intended to provide the commercial fishery with greater flexibility by no longer requiring full payback of annual catch limit (ACL) overages when the Atlantic spiny dogfish stock is considered healthy.

entry.title: US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: MONROE, NY – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited six construction employers for willful and serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at the site of a planned 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building and proposed a combined $648,094 in penalties. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an allegation of struck-by and collapse hazards associated with a large excavation at the Monroe Commons project – also known as Magna Square development – a planned 4-story, approximately 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building with retail, office space, and a 39-room hotel located on an 18-acre site. The excavation had a steep, unstable embankment nearly 75 feet high which was not adequately sloped or shored. OSHA issued a total of 23 serious and five willful citations to the project’s general contractor and five subcontractors for failing to protect employees from cave-in, struck-by, and chemical hazards; neglecting to shield employees from falling or rolling rock and soil from an excavation face; and not ensuring daily inspections of excavations were conducted by a competent person. Advanced Plan and Build LLC, and subcontractors Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. – operating as Drip Drop Waterproofing Inc. – and The Paving Masters LLC received citations for willfully exposing employees to cave-in and struck-by hazards from an unprotected excavation. OSHA also cited Advanced Plan and Build and The Paving Masters for their willful failure to ensure that the excavation, which was between 21 and 75 feet deep, was designed by a registered professional engineer. Subcontractors Century Max Industries Corp., DelValle Contractor, and Prime Structure Inc. were cited for serious violations for failing to protect employees from cave-in and struck-by hazards. DelValle and Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. also received citations for serious violations related to lack of fall protection and chemical hazards.OSHA proposed the following penalties: Advanced Plan and Build LLC—$175,444; Century Max Industries Corp.—$46,340; DelValle Contractor—$19,151; Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc.—$198,615; Prime Structure Inc.—$19,860; and The Paving Masters LLC—$188,684. The employers have 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: Blindness Awareness Month - October — Governor of Maine — Official Documents (Executive Orders)
entry.content:
WHEREAS, blindness and low vision affect millions of Americans, including an estimated 35,000 Maine people; and 

WHEREAS, the white cane and guide dog serve as essential tools that promote independence, mobility, and safety for people who are blind or have low vision, and Maine law recognizes their use and provides protections for people who use them; and 

WHEREAS, people who are blind and or low vision contribute significantly to the social, cultural, and economic vitality of our state as they pursue meaningful careers in diverse professions, strengthen Maine's workforce, raise families, and enrich our communities through their participation in all aspects of life; and 

WHEREAS, we honor the resilience, wisdom, and lifelong contributions of older adults who are blind or have low vision, and their efforts to maintain independence while navigating the unique challenges of aging with vision loss; and 

WHEREAS, people with vision loss continue to encounter stigma, discrimination, and accessibility barriers, including misconceptions about their capabilities and needs; and 

WHEREAS, we recognize the efforts of vision rehabilitation professionals, educators, self-advocates, and allies across Maine who work to advance equality, accessibility and opportunities for people who are blind or have low vision; and 

WHEREAS, Blindness Awareness Month calls attention to the importance of accessibility, inclusion, and respect, and reminds us of the progress achieved through advocacy, education, and civil rights protections, as well as the work still to be done; 

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as 

Blindness Awareness Month

in Maine, and I call upon all residents to join in recognizing the contributions of Maine people who are blind or have low vision and to work together to promote accessibility, inclusion, independence, and full participation in all aspects of community life.

Using the New Call Center Phone Menu

Oct 14, 2026

As previously communicated, on October 12, MaineCare launched a new interactive voice response (IVR) system, Gabby, to enhance the provider self-service experience and help callers to Provider Services access information more quickly and efficiently. 

Gabby can assist with five common inquiry types: 

  • Claim Status 
  • Prior Authorizations 
  • Member Eligibility
  • Payments
  • Provider Enrollment 

When you call, simply tell Gabby which of these topics best matches your reason for calling. Depending on your inquiry, Gabby will ask for basic information, such as your NPI, Tax ID, or a member ID, to verify your request. Please have this information ready before you call so that you can quickly provide it to Gabby. Gabby will prompt multiple times for the information it needs to proceed. If you do not provide a valid response, Gabby will disconnect. 

Once your information is validated, Gabby will guide you through additional prompts to help you obtain the information you need. 

If your inquiry is not related to one of the self-service options listed above, tell Gabby "other" to connect with a customer service representative for further assistance. You can ask to speak to customer service representative or agent at any time. 

In addition, to give providers expanded time for support, on Thursday, October 15, 2026, the Call Center will be open until 7:00 PM. 

As a reminder, in addition to calling Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585, you can also email MaineCareprovider@gainwelltechnologies.com. For MaineCare Partner Portal issues, you can email MaineCaresupport@gainwelltechnologies.com.

Reminder: Maine eCourts in Region 6 (Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County) Virtual Presentation Today at Noon

Date: 10/14/2026

To help attorneys and other stakeholders in Region 6 get ready for eFiling, the Judicial Branch will hold a virtual presentation by Zoom today.

Topic: Maine eCourts in Region 6: Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County
Date & Time: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.
Please click the link below to join the webinar:
https://courts-maine-gov.zoom.us/j/96415858276
Passcode: 522889

The Zoom presentation will be recorded and posted on the Maine eCourts Training & Resources page following the live session.

District and Superior Courts in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo counties (comprising Judicial Region 6) will transition from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) on Monday, December 7, 2026. This includes all case types in the Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs) and Superior Courts; and in the Belfast, Rockland, West Bath, and Wiscasset District Courts.

Who Is Required to eFile?
Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

For more information about Maine eCourts visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

To receive updates from the Maine Judicial Branch on Maine eCourts and other news, sign up for our mailing list at: https://www.courts.maine.gov/news/signup.html

Title IV PostsecondaryInstitutions: Workforce Pell Program Applications Open for Second Review Cycle Through Nov. 13

October 14, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist | media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA -The State Workforce Development Board(SWDB) is accepting applications from Title IV postsecondary institutionsseeking stateapproval to offer programs eligible for federal Workforce Pell Grants. Applications for the second review cycle are due Friday, Nov. 13

Maine's Workforce Pell application provides an online process for eligible postsecondary institutions to seek approval to offer short-term workforce training programs that meet federal Workforce Pell Grant requirements. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly by the SWDB.

Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage and in-demand careers. States are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before they are submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state,"said Vaughan Woodruff, chair of the State Workforce Development Board."The program's support for training that connects people with skills needed for Maine's workforce presents a significant opportunity for Maine workers and employers."

The Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy establishesthe state's process foridentifying, reviewing and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. The policy was developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System and University of MaineSystem.

"Workforce Pell brings a new source of federal funding to Maine's short-term workforce training programs," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "We are excited to help Maine's postsecondary institutions take advantage of this opportunity to strengthen their programs, reach more students and prepare Maine's workforce for the future."

The SWDB will evaluate applications and make recommendations to the Governor for state certification. Programs certified by the Governor will then be submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval. Following federal approval, the SWDB will publish the list of Maine-certified Workforce Pell programs on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage within 30 days.

Institutions can find the Workforce Pell application, eligibility requirements, program guidance and additional information on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage.

The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF.

At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services.

entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $81.5 million in funding to address the critical workforce needs of employers in high-growth and emerging industries across the Appalachian, Delta, and Northern Border regions. entry.title: US Department of Labor announces field assistance bulletin withdrawing 3 opinion letters on tipped employees — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division today announced the issuance of a new field assistance bulletin addressing the treatment of related duties performed by tipped employees under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Field Assistance Bulletin No. 2026-1 brings the division’s guidance on tipped employees with dual jobs into alignment with current regulations.The bulletin withdraws the division’s 1979, 1980, and 1985 opinion letters concerning the application of dual jobs regulations to tipped employees. The withdrawal of the three opinion letters is necessary because they no longer reflect the division’s policy or interpretation of the FLSA. The bulletin also clarifies that the current dual jobs regulation focuses on whether an employee performs duties related to the employee’s tipped occupation, rather than imposing a specific percentage-based limit on the time an employee may spend performing related, non-tipped duties within that occupation.The publication of the new bulletin follows a 2024 federal court decision that vacated the department’s 2021 dual jobs final rule. After that decision, the department removed the regulatory text adopted under the 2021 rule and reinstated the original dual jobs regulations.The new field assistance bulletin clarifies that no current Wage and Hour Division guidance relies on the former percentage-based limit on the time a tipped employee may spend performing related, non-tipped duties, commonly known as the 80/20 rule. The division removed its 80/20 rule guidance from its Field Operations Handbook in January 2025, and the handbook is now consistent with the reinstated 1967 dual jobs regulations.As noted in the most recent regulatory agenda, the department is developing a notice of proposed rulemaking to amend various regulations for tipped employees under the FLSA. The department welcomes public comments on the proposed rule once it is published.Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including the agency’s enforcement of tip regulations under the FLSA.Read Field Assistance Bulletin No. 2026-1.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $95.5M in grants to support innovative programs for reskilling, reemploying dislocated workers — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $95.5 million in funding to support the creation of innovative models of training and employment services that connect workers affected by layoffs to high-growth industries.Administered by the department’s Employment and Training Administration, Rapid Reskill Dislocated Worker Grants support 20 projects across 17 states to quickly connect workers affected by layoffs to employment and training services that lead to high-wage, in-demand occupations in industries expected to grow, including domestic manufacturing, aerospace, energy production, construction, and other occupations important to reindustrialization.Reskill DWG projects are designed to swiftly assess participants’ prior experience and existing skillsets and chart a course to an in-demand occupation or industry. Participants will gain industry-specific skills and credentials to speed their reemployment while projects will develop and share innovative approaches for connecting workers impacted by layoffs with careers in America’s growth industries.“The Rapid Reskill Grants support our commitment to ensuring displaced workers have the skills they need to pursue the American Dream,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “They also help ensure a workforce for the Golden Age of reindustrialization and empower workers to stay rooted in their hometown.”Reskill DWGs aim to rapidly place dislocated workers into paid work, whether full-time unsubsidized employment, a Registered Apprenticeship, or other paid, structured on-the-job training in their target occupation or industry within six months of enrollment. Toward that end, these innovative projects incorporate short-term, intensive training programs that lead to industry-recognized credentials and skills development aligned with industry-specific or occupational training. entry.title: Consent judgment orders California-based home appliance company to pay $800K to 339 employees denied overtime pay — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: LOS ANGELES – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment requiring a home appliance company to pay $800,000 in back wages and damages to 339 employees after an investigation found the company violated federal wage laws.The judgment comes after the department’s Wage and Hour Division investigated Coway USA Inc. and found that the employer paid employees on a piece-rate basis and failed to pay employees for time spent attending mandatory meetings, picking up and loading supplies, and performing work before and after their shifts, in violation of the Fair Labor Standards Act. Investigators also found that Coway did not include nondiscretionary incentives, bonuses, and commissions in overtime pay calculations and frequently reduced the number of hours employees recorded working on their timecards.Entered in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California on Sept. 9, the consent judgment requires Coway to record all hours the implicated employees worked, including time they spend picking up supplies, attending mandatory training, and communicating with customers before and after appointments. Coway is also required to give employees pay statements that show their hours worked, services provided to customers, and the rate Coway paid for the hours and services. The consent judgment orders Coway USA Inc. to pay $400,000 in unpaid overtime wages and an equal amount in damages to 339 employees working in the greater metro areas of Los Angeles, New York City, and Washington, D.C. The company also agreed to pay $10,000 in penalties for willful violations. Coway USA Inc. is a subsidiary of Coway Co. Ltd., a multinational company specializing in home appliances. The company installs and maintains various appliances, including water and air filtration products throughout the U.S.Employers and employees can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division.The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the Fair Labor Standards Act, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act.

entry.title: US departments of Labor, Health and Human Services expand efforts to help employees access health benefits — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The departments of Labor and Health and Human Services announced that representatives from several large employers with self-insured health plans signed a statement of support for the expansion of electronic prior authorization reform to the self-insured markets. “The departments appreciate these U.S. companies for stepping forward to collaborate with Labor and Health and Human Services to help employees cut through red tape and receive their health benefits,” said Assistant Secretary for Employee Benefits Security Daniel Aronowitz. “By signing this statement of support for the expansion of electronic prior authorization reform, government and private industry are working together on behalf of the American workforce.”Signed by five delegates from Amazon, Axon Enterprise Inc., Google, Meta, and Oracle Corp., the statement supports the June 2025 Prior Authorization Pledge, which contains six key reforms, including standardizing all prior authorization submissions, reducing the volume of medical procedures that require preapproval, and making sure medical professionals review all clinical denials. It also asks third party administrators to enhance transparency and communication around authorization decisions and appeals.“Patients and doctors shouldn’t have to fall back on faxes and paperwork simply because of how a patient’s health plan is funded,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “We’ve brought insurers, providers, and technology companies to the table to modernize prior authorization, and now employers are helping us take another important step. When the entire healthcare system moves together, we can spend less time on paperwork and more time getting patients the care they need.”Over the past year, the Trump Administration and industry partners have implemented electronic prior authorization reforms. In 2025, leading insurance companies signed the Prior Authorization Pledge to improve the process for their Medicare Advantage, Medicaid Managed Care, Health Insurance Marketplace, and commercial plans. Read the employer statement of support.

entry.title: US Department of Labor cites Illinois utility construction company for repeated exposure to trenching hazards — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Frankfort-based utility construction company for repeatedly exposing employees to excavation safety hazards after federal investigators observed employees working in an unprotected trench.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration initiated an investigation of Always Underground LLC as part of its National Emphasis Program on Trenching after witnessing employees working in an unprotected trench deeper than eight feet.OSHA cited the employer for three repeat violations for failing to provide workers with a safe means of egress, to install a trench protective system that would protect against cave-ins, and to keep excavated or other materials and equipment at least 2 feet from the edge. Additionally, the agency cited the employer for a serious violation for failing to provide workers with protective hardhats against falling objects.In total, OSHA proposed $380,664 in penalties.The employer has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: US Department of Labor secures court order requiring New Jersey employer to pay $700K in back wages, damages to 48 workers denied overtime pay — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: VOORHEES, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment and final order in federal district court requiring a New Jersey drywall installer to pay $725,000 in back wages, damages, and civil money penalties after denying 48 workers overtime pay.The department’s Wage and Hour Division found that P & B Partitions Inc. failed to pay their employees for pre-shift work while they waited for transportation to their jobsites. The failure to pay constitutes a violation under the Fair Labor Standards Act’s overtime provisions. “Tasks completed to prepare for the job, and in this case, while waiting to get to the worksite, is work that must be compensated,” said Wage and Hour Division District Director Charlene Rachor in Southern New Jersey. “Failing to pay workers overtime wages deprives them of their rights, and we will hold employers accountable for such actions.”The consent judgment requires P & B Partitions Inc. to pay $350,000 in back wages, an equal amount in liquidated damages to 48 workers, and requires payment of an additional $25,000 in civil penalties. The judgment was entered in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey on June 26, 2026.“The U.S. Department of Labor will pursue legal action to ensure that all employees receive the compensation they are legally owed,” said Regional Solicitor of Labor Jeffrey S. Rogoff in New York. “This case demonstrates that employers can face costly consequences if they do not comply with federal wage law.”Employees and employers can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act.Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including how workers can use a search tool if they believe they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free WorkWise Timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

entry.title: US Department of Labor, US Trade Representative secure another USMCA enforcement victory in Amphenol case — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The United States today announced the successful resolution of the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRM) matter at the Amphenol Optimize México, S.A. de C.V. facility located in Nogales, Sonora, Mexico, which manufactures automotive and aerospace connectors, cables, and components. The resolution is another win for the Trump Administration, whose America First approach ensures our trade partners do not undermine worker protections to gain an unfair trade advantage or attract investment.The United States and Mexico agreed on a course of remediation to address labor rights violations occurring at the facility, including employer interference in union activity and retaliatory dismissals of workers. That plan has now been implemented, and the Denial of Rights concerns raised in the U.S. request for review have been remediated. As a result, the United States Trade Representative has directed the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility.The U.S. Department of Labor’s Bureau of International Labor Affairs, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, and the Mexican government facilitated a resolution with Amphenol to remediate workers’ claims.Actions taken by the facility to address the matter include: Reinstating nine workers with full backpay and benefits; Implementing a neutrality statement and guidelines related to the freedom of association and collective bargaining; andInstalling and publicizing a complaint mechanism through which workers can report violations of their rights and breaches of company policies.Actions taken by the Government of Mexico to address the matter include: Delivering in-person trainings for all company personnel on the freedom of association and collective bargaining; Monitoring the facility and engaging with workers and the company throughout its review period; andMaintaining a direct email address, reporting platform, and telephone line for workers to anonymously report any potential acts of unlawful interference or other violations of freedom of association and collective bargaining rights, and timely investigating any allegations.The RRM, developed under the first Trump administration, is an unprecedented trade tool that works to level the playing field for American workers by addressing weak labor law enforcement in Mexican workplaces that compete in trade with the U.S. BackgroundThe United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On April 11, 2025, the ILC received an RRM petition from the Sindicato Industrial Operaciones y Manufacturas, a Mexican labor union. The petition alleged that Amphenol had violated workers’ right to freedom of association and collective bargaining by coercing workers to vote for the company-favored outcome during a union vote, discouraging workers from joining an independent union, and taking reprisals against workers due to their union preferences, including through dismissals. The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. The ILC determined that there was sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms.As a result, on May 9, 2025, the United States Trade Representative submitted a request to Mexico to review the matter. Mexico accepted the request, conducted an investigation, and worked with Amphenol to provide remediation to dismissed workers and implement facility-wide measures aimed at safeguarding freedom of association and collective bargaining rights. The United States has reviewed the matter and concluded the situation to have been remediated. As a result of the above actions taken by the facility and Mexico to resolve the action, the United States agrees that there is no ongoing denial of rights. Ambassador Greer’s letter directing the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility is available here.Read the full course of remediation here.Read an unofficial courtesy Spanish translation of the full course of remediation here.Information about previous requests can be found here.Learn more about the department’s work to make global competition fair for American workers.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago Grants to promote mine safety, health education — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago grant funding to two organizations to support education and training initiatives that will help identify and prevent unsafe working conditions in and around the nation’s mines.Administered by the department’s Mine Safety and Health Administration, the Brookwood-Sago Mine Safety grant program helps recipients create training materials, conduct mine safety training, and educational programs designed to protect the safety and health of miners. In awarding the grants, MSHA focused on innovative plans for mine safety and pilot programs that may be useful for miners working in a broad range of positions. The grants also put an emphasis on programs and materials targeting workers in smaller mines that train mine operators and miners about MSHA standards, and emergency response training.Established under the Mine Improvement and New Emergency Response Act of 2006, the grant program honors the miners lost at the Jim Walter Resources #5 mine in Brookwood, Alabama, on Sept. 23, 2001, and at the Sago Mine in Buckhannon, West Virginia, on Jan. 2, 2006.The recipients of the 2026 Brookwood-Sago grants are as follows:RecipientCityState/TerritoryAmountSaelua Medical Corporation Pago PagoAmerican Samoa$170,000University of ArizonaTucsonAZ$80,000

entry.title: US Department of Labor obtains consent order against retirement plan fiduciaries of defunct Chicago law firm for failing to distribute $6.4M in assets — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: CHICAGO – Following a complaint filed by the U.S. Department of Labor, a defunct Chicago law firm’s retirement plan distributed $6,498,858 in retirement plan assets to 40 employees. The plan’s fiduciaries failed to properly terminate the plan and disburse those funds as required by law.On Aug. 18, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, entered a consent order resolving the department’s claims against the McCullough, Campbell & Lane LLP, and the firm’s capital partners David L. Joslyn, John W. McCullough, F. Dennis Nelson, and Paul S. Turner. The department alleged that the defendants violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act by failing to follow a 2019 partnership resolution. The resolution required them to terminate the firm’s retirement plan and distribute the plan’s assets to employees. The defendants have provided proof that plan’s assets were distributed to participants, except for approximately $13,861 in the employer-level plan accounts. The consent order requires the plan’s recordkeeper to distribute those funds to its participants and to terminate the plan. “After their law firm closed, Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn failed to provide employees with their promised retirement benefits,” said Employee Benefits Security Administration Regional Director Kelli Hammerl in Chicago. “The Department of Labor helped participants gain access to their retirement savings.” The order permanently bars Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn from serving as fiduciaries or service providers for any ERISA-covered employee benefit plan. The plan transferred account balances belonging to plan participants it could not locate to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation’s Missing Participants Program.Employers can get help complying with the law through EBSA’s correction programs, which includes the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program. The VFCP allows plan officials to correct violations and avoid excise taxes for prohibited transactions. Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.
